listeningGuides.intro: Sometimes it’s a voice that makes you want to hear another song. Here are singers from folk, pop, jazz, R&B and rock, on record and on stage.

listeningGuides.title: Korean indie: where to start
listeningGuides.description: Korean songs worth sharing, with live performances, artist stories and more music to try.
listeningGuides.intro: Some songs, live performances and a little about the people behind them. A place to start if Korean music is new to you.
paragraphs: There’s a love song by The Black Skirts, a farewell from YdBB and a live version of SE SO NEON’s The Wave that carries on long after the singing ends. You can dip in wherever you like.

You don’t need to know Korean to spend time here. Yerin Baek’s 0310 is sung in English, and there’s a little background for the other songs. More artists appear below, with new additions as the journal grows.

trackNotes.black-skirts: The Black Skirts is Bryan Cho’s solo project. EVERYTHING is a love song that first came out in 2016, before joining the album TEAM BABY a year later. The official music video is here, and the album is linked on his artist page if you’d like more.
trackNotes.yerin-baek: 0310 is sung in English, with lyrics on screen in Yerin Baek’s own video. It comes from Every letter I sent you., an album she describes as a collection of thoughts and memories from ages nineteen to twenty-three. Square (2017) is another song from the same record.
trackNotes.ydbb: YdBB are a five-piece band built around singer-songwriter Yu Dabin, playing music that moves between acoustic folk and rock. ONCE is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. It’s a farewell she talks about in the band’s release interview.
trackNotes.hanroro: In Even if you leave, HANRORO writes about the things that are hard to let go of. Her release note describes being caught between blaming someone else and blaming yourself, and trying to get through the day without making that feeling worse.
trackNotes.se-so-neon: Hwang Soyoon’s voice and guitar are at the centre of SE SO NEON’s The Wave. This version was filmed at the 2020/NEON concert in December 2019. After the last vocal line, the performance carries on with a long instrumental ending.
